newsitem.title: CHINA: China's PLA more popular than new HK legislature.
newsitem.headline: China's PLA more popular than new HK legislature.

text.p: China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) received a surprise 70th birthday present from Hong Kong on Friday in the form of an opinion poll that showed the garrison was more popular than the territory's new legislature.

Nearly 30 percent of those polled in the survey by the Chinese University of Hong Kong said they were satisfied with the PLA's performance, while only 17.6 percent felt satisfied with the Provisional Legislature.
Only 5.7 percent felt dissatisfied with the PLA, while 34.5 percent felt dissatisfied with the legislature. The remaining respondents answered "don't know".
The new government fared well in the poll with a general satisfaction rating of 65 percent.
Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years, was reabsorbed by China on July 1 as a special administrative region.
The PLA replaced British troops as the garrison, and an unelected, China-appointed legislature was installed.
The government is led by former shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa, who was appointed by China to take over from Chris Patten, Britain's last colonial governor.

Many people in Hong Kong have misgivings about the PLA because of its role in the 1989 anti-democracy crackdown in Beijing. But the army, which marked its 70th anniversary on Friday, has kept a low profile here since its arrival.
The poll interviewed 585 people by telephone last week.
